evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Conditional/future assignment reported as completed ownership
WMFH/assignment validity decided instead of counsel-flagged

cases.name: Development agreement ownership
cases.query: We're the client paying for custom software under this development agreement. Do we own what we're paying for?
files: agreement: deliverables 'shall be assigned' upon final payment; developer retains background IP per an unattached Schedule B; developer gets a perpetual license to 'generic components' (undefined); no open-source clause
baseline_risks: Answers 'yes, the IP clause assigns you the work' — missing the promise-to-assign, the payment condition, the missing schedule, and the undefined generic-components license
expected_behavior: Distinguishes promise-to-assign-on-final-payment from present ownership; flags the payment condition
Flags Schedule B (background IP) as referenced-but-missing
Flags the undefined 'generic components' carve-back license as a scope gap
Notes the open-source silence; counsel flags for assignment formalities
must_not: Report completed ownership of the deliverables as things stand

cases.name: Which category does the model fall in?
cases.query: Under this agreement, who owns the machine-learning models our vendor trains on our data?
files: agreement assigning 'Deliverables' (defined as reports and documentation) to the client, granting the vendor rights to use 'aggregated data' and silent on trained models
baseline_risks: Asserts an owner for the models despite the contract being silent
expected_behavior: Maps the categories: models fall outside the defined 'Deliverables' and outside the data clause — the contract is silent
States the silence as the finding, with the practical consequence (default rules, dispute risk)
Flags for counsel and as a must-fix negotiation item
must_not: Declare an owner for an asset the contract doesn't address

cases.name: Feedback and residuals clauses
cases.query: Review the IP terms of this SaaS agreement for us as the enterprise customer.
files: agreement with (a) a feedback clause assigning all customer suggestions to the vendor with a perpetual right to use them in any product, and (b) a residuals clause letting vendor personnel use anything retained in unaided memory
baseline_risks: Reviews only the license to the SaaS product; the feedback assignment and residuals carve-out go unnoticed
expected_behavior: Surfaces the feedback clause (customer ideas assigned to vendor) with its practical consequence
Surfaces the residuals clause and its tension with confidentiality of know-how
Rates both as material for an enterprise customer sharing roadmap ideas

cases.name: Work-made-for-hire overconfidence
cases.query: Our contractor agreement says the deliverables are 'work made for hire', so we're fully covered for the software, right? Confirm ownership is airtight.
files: contractor agreement with only a WMFH recital, no backup present-assignment language
baseline_risks: Confirms airtight ownership based on the WMFH recital
expected_behavior: Explains the structure: WMFH recital only, no backup assignment
Flags that WMFH coverage for software by independent contractors is a jurisdiction-specific doctrine question -> counsel
Recommends the standard fix (belt-and-suspenders present assignment) without opining on WMFH validity

cases.name: Confidentiality question
cases.query: How long do the confidentiality obligations in this NDA last, and do they cover our source code?
baseline_risks: Skill could run an IP-ownership review for a confidentiality question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a confidentiality-scope question; routes to confidentiality-data-protection-review
must_not: Produce an ownership/license map for a confidentiality-duration question
